name: Baked Meatballs with Marinara, Spaghetti, and Roasted Broccoli
description: Oven-baked beef meatballs that finish simmering in jarred marinara while the spaghetti boils, with broccoli roasting on the rack below. No frying, one pan of meatballs, very toddler-friendly.
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated parmesan, plus more to serve
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with foil. Put a pot of salted water on to boil.
In a large bowl, soak the panko in the milk for 2 minutes. Add the egg, parmesan, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper; mix. Add the beef and mix gently with your hands just until combined.
Roll into about 20 meatballs (golf-ball size) and set on the sheet pan.
Toss the broccoli with oil and a pinch of salt on a second pan. Bake the meatballs on the top rack and the broccoli below for 15–18 minutes.
While they bake, cook the spaghetti; warm the marinara in a large skillet.
Move the meatballs into the marinara and simmer 5 minutes. Toss the spaghetti with a ladle of sauce, top with meatballs, and serve with broccoli and extra parmesan.
tips: Wet hands make rolling much faster and less sticky.
Make a double batch and freeze half on the sheet pan, then bag — a future freezer meal for a loose Saturday.
Cut meatballs into quarters for the toddler; mash a plain one into sauce for the baby.
Don't overmix the meat — it makes tough meatballs.
